blocks.text: Kehrer Verlag publishes Kashmir, the Valley by Robert Nickelsberg . The book will be presented, with a signing session, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 4 p.m. at the Kehrer Verlag booth at Paris Photo .

In 1989, as a popular uprising against Indian rule began in Jammu and Kashmir, American photographer Robert Nickelsberg started documenting the unfolding conflict while working as a contract photographer for Time magazine from New Delhi. Over the following twenty-two years, he repeatedly returned to the region, building an extensive visual record of a conflict shaped by the longstanding rivalry between India and Pakistan.

From 1989 to 2011, Nickelsberg captured demonstrations, funerals, military operations, militant groups, religious rituals, elections, displacement and ordinary life. His access extended across the Line of Control into Pakistan-administered territory, allowing him to document the conflict from both sides.

Kashmir, the Valley brings together this long-term body of work, following the conflict through militarization, destruction and displacement while remaining closely attentive to the people living within its consequences. Muslim families, Hindu Pandits, soldiers, local politicians, children and pilgrims inhabit the same visual landscape, where checkpoints, armed searches, mourning and uncertainty become part of everyday experience.

Nickelsberg documented the evolution of the conflict as India and Pakistan developed and adapted their respective strategies, continually testing the limits of confrontation while stopping short of outright war. His photographs reveal the consequences of these shifting policies on the ground. To this day, caught between the competing interests of the two countries, the people of Indian-administered Kashmir remain vulnerable to violence largely beyond their control.

Across more than two decades, Nickelsberg’s photographs trace not only political and military upheaval, but the ways in which conflict becomes embedded in the fabric of everyday life. They offer a sustained portrait of Kashmir’s people and places, where displacement, loss and uncertainty exist alongside work, worship, family and ordinary routines.

The book is accompanied by essays by Robert Nickelsberg, Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist and author Steve Coll, and Kashmiri novelist Mirza Waheed. Together, they bring photographic testimony into dialogue with historical and political context and lived experience from within Kashmir.

Robert Nickelsberg worked as a Time magazine contract photographer for nearly 30 years, specializing in political and cultural change in developing countries. He is the author of Afghanistan – A Distant War (Prestel, 2013) and Afghanistan’s Heritage: Restoring Spirit and Stone (2018). His previous book with Kehrer Verlag, Legacy of Lies: El Salvador 1981–1984 , was published in 2024 and brought together a collection of black and white images shot for Time magazine during the civil war in El Salvador in the early 1980s.
